# Person paths from Agastya witnesses

This is a shortest-path audit over sourced person-to-person claim edges. All six source-local Agastya facets start at distance zero. Text witnesses, places, and citations remain visible in the 3D graph but are not counted as person hops. Direction is ignored only when finding a path. A path does not show that its people met or lived at the same time.

## 3 hops · 771 people

### Abhaya · Dhṛtarāṣṭra’s son in the CE birth-order roster

Agastya · Mahābhārata → Yudhiṣṭhira → Dhṛtarāṣṭra · Viṣṇu Purāṇa 4.20 witness → Abhaya · Dhṛtarāṣṭra’s son in the CE birth-order roster

- C030: Yudhiṣṭhira → asks about → Agastya · Mahābhārata. [Mahābhārata, Vana Parva, Ganguli §96, Vana §96](https://sacred-texts.com/hin/m03/m03096.htm). translation_checked. Yudhiṣṭhira asks why Agastya killed Vātāpi. He asks Lomaśa, not Agastya; no meeting is asserted.
- MB2ROSTER_003: Dhṛtarāṣṭra · Viṣṇu Purāṇa 4.20 witness → attends rajasuya of → Yudhiṣṭhira. [Mahābhārata, Book 2 (Sabhāparvan), Section XXXIII: Rājasūya guests arrive, §XXXIII, p. 71](https://sacred-texts.com/book/the-mahabharata-book-2-sabha-parva/section-xxxiii). translation_checked. Dhṛtarāṣṭra is individually named among those who came to Yudhiṣṭhira’s Rājasūya sacrifice. Kuru elder and guest
- MBAR117: Abhaya · Dhṛtarāṣṭra’s son in the CE birth-order roster → son of → Dhṛtarāṣṭra · Viṣṇu Purāṇa 4.20 witness. [Mahābhārata, Ādiparvan, BORI Critical Edition electronic text, Mahābhārata Ādiparvan 1.108.12](https://bombay.indology.info/mahabharata/text/UR/MBh01.txt). translation_checked. Abhaya is named in the sequence of Dhṛtarāṣṭra’s sons. The CE asks for Dhṛtarāṣṭra’s sons by name and says the roster follows their birth order (1.108.1, 15). Paired dual forms and the triple Dṛḍharatha are represented as distinct people by Sanskrit number; repeated exact names are handled as unresolved references.

## Method and limits

- `translation_checked` concerns a passage in translation, not historicity.
- `editorial_attribution` includes assigned hymn speakers and related interpretive links.
- Co-mention or an attributed poetic lineage is weaker than a narrated encounter; read every step of a path.
- The path list is limited by the presently reviewed corpus and should grow with more editions and texts.
